prompt: Write 10 distinct short extracts of Larkmere Mutual's official guidance, procedures or policy wording about: waiting for the loss adjuster. Two to four sentences each, in the society's own formal voice. Use type "fact". Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"If we appoint a loss adjuster, please wait for them to contact you before arranging permanent repairs. They may need to inspect the damage, take photographs, and confirm the cause and extent of the loss. Delaying repairs until that visit helps us assess your claim fairly."},{"type":"fact","content":"You should keep the damaged property in its current state wherever it is safe to do so, until the loss adjuster has attended. If urgent steps are needed to make the home secure or prevent further damage, you may take those steps first. Please keep any receipts and tell us what you have done."},{"type":"fact","content":"The loss adjuster may need access to all affected rooms, contents, and any areas where water, smoke, or storm damage has travelled. If you are not available when the visit is arranged, let us know as soon as possible so that a new appointment can be made. Repeated missed appointments may delay progress on the claim."},{"type":"fact","content":"Do not throw away damaged items before the loss adjuster has had the opportunity to inspect them, unless there is a health or safety reason to do so. Where disposal is unavoidable, please take clear photographs and retain samples if possible. This helps us understand what was lost and what can be settled."},{"type":"fact","content":"If a contractor has already attended to carry out emergency work, please tell the loss adjuster what was done and when. The loss adjuster will usually want to see the damage before any full repair starts, unless we have agreed otherwise. Their report forms part of our decision on your claim."},{"type":"fact","content":"While you are waiting for the loss adjuster, please continue to protect the property from further damage. This may include switching off water, covering broken windows, or moving belongings to a dry area. Such temporary measures do not count as a permanent repair."},{"type":"fact","content":"The loss adjuster acts on our behalf to gather information about the claim and may ask questions about how the loss happened. Please answer as fully and accurately as you can. If you have photographs, invoices, or police references, have them ready for the visit or send them when requested."},{"type":"fact","content":"If the loss adjuster needs specialist inspection, such as for subsidence, escape of water, or hidden structural damage, the claim may remain open for longer. In those cases, please wait for our instruction before authorising further work.
